summary: Backend-only tests for FreshCuts SEED_VERSION=5 additions: (a) Subscription system (public /boxes + auth POST/GET/pause/DELETE), (b) Product.cut_images dict on Onions/Potatoes/etc., (c) Product.recipes on ready-mix items. Extended /app/backend/tests/test_freshcuts_api.py with 11 new tests across two new classes (TestProductEnrichment, TestSubscriptions) while preserving all 30 prior tests. Result: 41/41 PASS (100%). All 10 scenarios from the review request are verified: /subscriptions/boxes returns essentials+mixed+premium with items[] and prices; POST /subscriptions with valid pincode creates active sub (box_name='Mixed Veg + Fruits', price_per_box=999, 7 box_items, next_delivery set); invalid pincode -> 400; missing auth -> 401; GET returns user's subs; pause -> status='paused'; DELETE -> status='cancelled'; Onions.cut_images has sliced/diced/shredded/grated URLs; Stir-fry Mix & Biryani Veggie Mix each expose one recipe with title/time_mins/servings/image/ingredients/steps; and all pre-existing endpoints (auth, products, pincodes, orders, Stripe payments, admin RBAC/CRUD) still pass unchanged.

minor.issue: next_delivery is computed as datetime.now() + min(days_ahead, 3) — the min() with 3 caps weekly (7d) and biweekly (14d) both to 3 days. This is likely a bug: biweekly subscribers will see the same next-delivery window as weekly. Suggest replacing min(days_ahead, 3) with just days_ahead (or make the first-delivery lead time a separate constant, e.g. first delivery = min(3, days_ahead), then subsequent = days_ahead).
(carried from prior iteration) Stripe still rejects amounts below its $0.50 minimum; total < ~₹48 -> 500. Consider server-side min-total enforcement for payment_method=stripe.

action_items: (Optional, likely bug) Fix next_delivery computation in POST /api/subscriptions: `min(days_ahead, 3)` collapses biweekly (14d) to 3d. Either drop min() or split into initial_lead_days vs cycle_days.
(Optional) BOXES is defined as a module-level dict — consider persisting boxes in Mongo (db.subscription_boxes) so admins can edit prices/items without a code deploy.
(Optional) Subscription lifecycle: no way to resume a paused subscription; consider adding POST /subscriptions/{id}/resume that sets status back to 'active'.

(Optional/security) Same as prior iteration — order & (now) subscription creation trust client-supplied address/phone with no server-side sanity checks; and product prices in orders are still client-supplied.

(Nice-to-have) Add DELETE /subscriptions/{id} hard-delete option or a paid_boxes counter — right now the DELETE endpoint soft-cancels which is fine but the HTTP verb is a bit misleading (behavior != REST-standard delete).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:490 — `next_delivery = datetime.now(...) + timedelta(days=min(days_ahead, 3))` — min() defeats the biweekly branch (see minor issue).
server.py subscriptions POST returns the sub with next_delivery as an aware datetime while stored as isoformat string — round-trip via Subscription(**doc) works today but is fragile.
server.py has grown from ~490 to ~530 lines with subscriptions — still below the 700 threshold; when it grows further, split routes/models by domain (auth, products, subscriptions, orders, payments).
BOXES pricing/items are hardcoded in server.py; no admin endpoint to edit — flagged for future admin surface.
Subscription and Order both accept client-supplied phone/address with no format validation (E.164, min length).
